statement: The Gazebo decode-rate conflict (5.2% in the 10-episode camdr batch vs 98.3% in the ep0 probe) is a lighting-DR flag wiring bug in the batch runner, not a vision failure.
safety: S0 sim only. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty for every run. No Pi, ssh, deploy, car, wheels or motor command. No existing rl/runs or explore/results file overwritten; no code edited.

runs.flags: --sensing camera_dr (pre-e47ccc3 code; no --student-shield flag; marker layout = pre-1be1015 12/9/13/14)
runs.note: Not reproduced at HEAD; see wiring and config analysis.

runs.flags: --sensing camera_dr --student-shield gazebo (matches the pre-e47ccc3 policy load: GAZEBO_GEAR shield); --marker-layout real (default)
runs.note: Frame and outcome counts match the original batch (22500 frames, 10 timeouts), but decode is 62% not 5.2%.
marker_layout is not recorded in the JSON; it is known only from the command line.

wiring_analysis.summary: camera_dr and --sensing camera --lighting-dr set the same effective photometric DR. The JSON photometric_dr field is misreported for camera_dr. The wiring is not the cause of the decode gap.
citations: simulation/gazebo/run_policy_episodes.py:152-153: camera_dr maps to sensing='camera', photometric=True inside GazeboBridge.__init__.
simulation/gazebo/run_policy_episodes.py:179: self.photometric = bool(photometric and sensing == 'camera'), which is True for camera_dr.
simulation/gazebo/vision_in_loop.py:449: self.dr = sample_dr(rng) if photometric else DRParams(). The photometric path draws DR params from the episode rng.
simulation/gazebo/vision_in_loop.py:471: apply_photometric_dr(img, self.dr, self.rng) runs on every frame.
simulation/gazebo/run_policy_episodes.py:551: main() passes photometric=args.lighting_dr, which is False for camera_dr without the flag. Line 153 overrides this for camera_dr.

simulation/gazebo/run_policy_episodes.py:559: photometric_dr=bool(args.lighting_dr and args.sensing.startswith('camera')). This is False for camera_dr without --lighting-dr, so the JSON misreports effective DR. Runs B and D show this.
simulation/gazebo/run_policy_episodes.py:476-487: --sensing camera_dr and --lighting-dr are the two ways to request photometric DR.

simulation/gazebo/run_policy_episodes.py:458-463 and :527-533: HEAD default --student-shield none loads StudentPolicy.load(shield=False). Earlier code (git show e47ccc3, removed lines) loaded gear=GAZEBO_GEAR unconditionally and labelled the controller 'student'.
simulation/gazebo/vision_in_loop.py:47 and :53: DEFAULT_LAYOUT='real', MARKER_IDS=(14,6,3). The pre-1be1015 code (commit 1be1015, 2026-11-13 19:11) used 12/9/13/14, which the batch (17:08) predates.

A_original_batch.shield: gazebo gear (inferred from git show e47ccc3)

wiring_analysis.probe_flags: The probe 'camera --lighting-dr' sets photometric=True through main() at :551 and the same VisionSensors path, so it matches camera_dr in effective DR. Their JSONs differ only in the photometric_dr label.

findings: The 98.3% figure appears in docs/archive/council_2026-11-14/01_gazebo_sim2sim_audit.md:138 and docs/archive/council_2026-11-14/07_cnn_lejepa_representations.md:70. Both cite docs/AGENT_BOARD.md [EXP] row.

docs/AGENT_BOARD.md is deleted in the working tree. At HEAD it is at line 83 (git show HEAD:docs/AGENT_BOARD.md), and its text says 'ep0 probe with --lighting-dr reached 98.3% decode'. This is a board note with no JSON.

explore/HISTORY.md:139 and :185 record the same figure as open. No JSON, log or frame artifact for the probe exists in rl/runs, explore/results or the archive. Greps for '98.3' and '0.983' in rl/runs found only unrelated files.
The probe was ep0 only, so its numerator and denominator (about 2250 frames if one episode) are unrecorded. Even if it reproduced, it is one episode, not a 10-episode batch.
The probe's flags, layout and shield at the time are not recorded, so it cannot be checked against the code.

verdict.hypothesis_status: NOT SUPPORTED as stated (wiring bug explains the gap). The wiring is not the cause of the decode conflict.
verdict.falsifier: decode stays under 20% with flags matched, or the gap is explained.
verdict.falsifier_literal_check: With flags matched (B vs C, identical effective photometric DR), decode is 45.6% and 48.2%. This is not under 20%. The falsifier's first clause is not met as written, so the test is inconclusive on that clause alone.
verdict.decisive_point: If the batch wiring were the cause, matching the flags should bring decode to about 98%. No run reaches 98%: the highest is 62.2% (D). The wiring hypothesis is refuted in its strict form, because the batch's flags were already effectively matched (see wiring_analysis).
verdict.gap_explained: partly. The 5.2% batch is not reproduced at HEAD. Known drift between the batch (2026-11-13 17:08) and HEAD: (1) policy shield, which changed from gazebo gear to none by default (e47ccc3); (2) marker constellation, which changed from 12/9/13/14 to 14/6/3 (1be1015); (3) aruco tracker (51f59c6, 2026-11-14, which touches the tracker path and not detect_gray; not tested). Matched configs give 30.3% (E, legacy layout) to 62.2% (D). Layout alone moves the rate by about 30 pp (D to E), but no tested config gives 5.2%. Residual is unexplained.
verdict.nondeterminism_note: B and C have the same effective config and differ in frames (2803 vs 2616), collisions/time and decode (45.6% vs 48.2%). Runs are therefore not bitwise reproducible at fixed seed, or some part of the config differs that the JSON does not record. This is a caveat for any single-batch decode number.
verdict.resolution: H-0006 should be closed as refuted for wiring, with the batch's 5.2% recorded as not reproducible at HEAD (config drift: shield, layout) and the 98.3% recorded as unverifiable. Do not use 98.3% as evidence.
not_done: Did not reproduce the batch with the exact 2026-11-13 code. Would need a git worktree at commit ee40bd7 or earlier, which I did not create.
Did not test the aruco tracker change 51f59c6 in isolation.
Did not test run-to-run repeatability at fixed config.

Did not change photometric_dr at run_policy_episodes.py:559. The brief allows only a trivial, default-off additive fix, and the JSON label fix is always-on, so I left it. Recommended fix: add photometric_effective=bridge.photometric to meta (additive key) or derive photometric_dr from the bridge after line 153. Owner decides.
